previous_deconvolution.verdict: Deconv CLint is LESS learnable than in vitro CLint

direct_clf_comparison.method: MMPK AUC → CL/F → SMILES prediction → analytical Cmax
direct_clf_comparison.verdict: Meta-learner gave zero weight to CL/F track

phase_0b.interpretation: Engine error has structural pattern (polar molecules under-predicted, bases over-predicted). However, this signal exists in the engine's fold error — not necessarily transferable to CLint deconvolution.

phase_0c.interpretation: Deconv CLint is 8x noisier than in vitro CLint and only weakly correlated (r=0.288). CLint absorbs errors from ALL parameters, inflating variance beyond what SMILES can predict.

overall_assessment: The proposed inverse PBPK is methodologically identical to the previous MMPK CLint deconvolution (brentq, same fixed parameters). That experiment yielded R²=0.166 < baseline 0.205. Phase 0B shows systematic engine error exists (TPSA, HBA, compound type), but Phase 0C shows this signal is destroyed when compressed into a single CLint variable (r=0.288, variance 8x). The systematic error pattern (polar under-prediction, base over-prediction) is better addressed by compound-type-specific model calibration or multi-parameter deconvolution, not single-variable CLint inversion.
actionable_finding: Engine fold error correlates with TPSA (r=-0.44) and compound type (base vs non-base). This could inform meta-learner stratification or engine-specific bias correction, but NOT through CLint inversion.
